intelligence.essence: Minimal Pumping-Witness Integrity Law: NayaNET may assert an unbounded fairness-debt upper bound from a minimized cycle witness only when the entry is independently reachable, the cycle is positively debt-producing and arbitrarily repeatable under all governing constraints, and a valid exit remains reachable after every finite repetition. Witness minimization shall preserve authority, scope, ordering, resource, terminal and evidence dependencies. A separate verifier shall reconstruct the certificate and distinguish model-level unbounded possibility from actual fairness violation or independently established system realizability. The standard: 'I found a very small explanation for why fairness debt could have grown without a finite bound. I can prove where the cycle begins, why it can repeat, what each repetition adds, and how the history can still end consistently with the observations. Another verifier can reconstruct that conclusion—and reject it immediately if I omitted a constraint.'
intelligence.falsifier: A short cycle presented as unboundedness proof without reachability/repeatability/exit proofs; a cycle that repeats only twice due to hidden finite budget presented as arbitrarily repeatable; minimization that drops authority/resource/temporal constraints; a pumping witness conflated with a proven fairness violation (different quantifiers: ∃h M(h)>K vs ∀h M(h)≥B_S); model-level unboundedness mislabeled as physical realizability; a fixed-suffix exit requirement falsely implying finiteness when varying exits exist.

human_view.meaning: A loop in a diagram is not proof of anything — the system needs a three-part certificate: how you get to the loop, why the loop can run forever, and how the story can still end. Each part has its own proof, and a separate verifier checks all of them without trusting the one who found the loop. The entry must be reachable from the real starting point. The cycle must add debt every time, never hit a hidden reset, and never run out of hidden fuel — the killer example is a loop that looks repeatable but consumes one of two retry tokens, dying on the third lap because the diagram forgot the budget. The exit must stay possible after any number of laps, not just after one. Then the certificate gets minimized — but minimization is constraint-preserving surgery, not log trimming: you may only remove what you prove irrelevant, and the minimized result gets independently rechecked. The IU*S example makes it concrete: any number of unserved rounds then one service gives final debt exactly zero but unbounded peak — and three histories (immediate service, late service, very late service) show why the verdict stays undetermined. The quantifier discipline is the moral center: 'for every bound there exists a history exceeding it' is not 'every history breaches the bound' — an unbounded peak can coexist with an undetermined fairness verdict, and a pumping witness is never a starvation accusation. Twelve adversarial fixtures, crowned by the finite-token mutation: a checker that sees only the scheduler state declares unboundedness; the correct checker sees the full state change and rejects, then accepts again once the artificial bound is removed and no other bound remains.

naya_view.directive: Never assert unboundedness from a loop alone. Prove entry reachability, positive debt gain, no-reset, arbitrary repeatability under the FULL state (budgets, authority, resources, time, lifecycle), and exit validity for every finite repetition count. Minimize only by constraint-preserving reduction; recheck the minimized certificate independently. Keep producer, verifier, and cold-verifier separate. Distinguish model-unboundedness from realizability and from proven violation. Prove W1–W12 with the finite-token mutation pair as the gate.

simple_view.meaning: A loop proves nothing until you prove you can reach it, repeat it forever without hidden limits, and still exit — then let someone else check your work.
